Vendor profile

Alibre

Alibre, LLC — Independent American Parametric 3D MCAD Developer (Alibre Design & Atom3D) Powered by Spatial ACIS

By GstarCAD Academy Engineering Editorial Board (Suzhou Gstarsoft Co., Ltd.) Reviewed by GstarCAD Academy Editorial Team Last reviewed 2026-10-26 Editorial Process

1. Corporate Independence: From 1997 Web-Collaborative CAD to Employee Buyout

Founded in 1997 in Richardson, Texas by Paul Grayson (former CEO of Micrografx), Alibre, Inc. originally pioneered internet-based distributed 3D CAD collaboration. Acquired by 3D printing giant 3D Systems in 2011 (rebranded temporarily as Geomagic Design), the core engineering leadership executed a management buyout in 2017 to re-establish Alibre, LLC as an independent, customer-focused MCAD vendor offering Alibre Design Expert and Atom3D.

2. Spatial ACIS Solid Kernel, Global Parameters & Excel-Driven Configurations

  • Spatial ACIS B-Rep Engine: Alibre Design utilizes Dassault Spatial's commercial ACIS kernel paired with D-Cubed 2D/3D constraint solvers, storing native parts (.AD_PRT), assemblies (.AD_ASM), and sheet metal (.AD_SMP) with perpetual standalone licensing options.
  • Global Parameter Files (.AD_GLP): Allows mechanical engineers to drive multi-part assembly clearances and bolt patterns from a single master equation table without requiring complex PDM server databases.

3. Companion 2D Production Drafting with GstarCAD 2027

While Alibre excels at low-cost 3D part modeling, its 2D drawing workspace (.AD_DRW) is not designed for large-scale facility layouts, electrical schematics, or high-speed AutoLISP batch automation. Machine shops routinely export Alibre views to native DWG/DXF and pair Alibre 3D with GstarCAD Mechanical for ISO/ASME shop-floor detailing and automated BOM generation.

When auditing Alibre, LLC (Richardson, TX, USA) software inside a multi-vendor engineering environment, CAD administrators and PLM architects must account for the following binary format, kernel tolerance, and API specifications:

5. Enterprise Co-Existence, Migration & TCO Optimization Protocol

In production supply chains where upstream 3D models or BIM containers originate from Alibre, LLC (Richardson, TX, USA) platforms, engineering IT directors optimize total cost of ownership (TCO) by deploying a tiered seat architecture centered on GstarCAD 2027 and DWG FastView:

  • Verified Data Exchange Pipeline: Export Alibre 3D parts via STEP AP242 (.stp) or ACIS (.sat) into GstarCAD 2027; export 2D layouts as AutoCAD 2018 DWG for high-speed shop-floor detailing and BOM ballooning in GstarCAD Mechanical.
  • Eliminating Redundant Seat Rentals: Rather than purchasing high-cost authoring subscriptions for project managers, site engineers, estimators, CNC operators, and quality inspectors who primarily review geometry or annotate 2D DWG/DXF sheets, organizations equip 70%–80% of their workforce with GstarCAD Perpetual Floating Licenses (GstarLM) and FastView 3D.
  • Automated Database Hygiene Before Transmittal: Prior to archiving project deliverables or importing external vendor DWG exports into corporate PDM/CDE vaults, run GstarCAD's batch script sequence (-PURGE RegApps → OVERKILL → AUDIT Yes → INDEXCTL = 3) to guarantee sub-second opening times and zero proxy object corruption.
